newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova's Dnestr separatists suspend OSCE contact.
newsitem.headline: Moldova's Dnestr separatists suspend OSCE contact.

text.p: Separatists in Moldova's Dnestr region have accused the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) of interfering in their affairs and have suspended its work in their self-proclaimed republic.

"We suspend the activities of the OSCE office in Tiraspol (the Dnestr capital)," said Valery Litkai, "foreign minister" of the breakaway Dnestr territory, in a letter quoted by Olvia-press news agency late on Monday.
The Dnestr separatists declared their region independent in 1990 but no country has recognised the Slav-dominated industrial heartland of Moldova as an independent state.

Hundreds of people were killed in a bloody conflict between Moldovan security forces and the separatists in 1992, halted only by the intervention of Russian troops. Russia keeps 6,000 troops in Dnestr, which borders Ukraine.
Moldova says it is ready to grant broad autonomy to the Dnestr, but separatist leaders insist on the region's full independence.

Litkai said the head of the OSCE mission in Moldova, Donald Johnson, was not welcome in Tiraspol. "Mr Johnson's appearance on our territory is considered inexpedient. Mr Johnson interferes in the Dnestr republic's internal affairs," he said.
The OSCE mission in Moldova declined to comment.
The separatist authorities were infuriated by Johnson's February report to the OSCE in Vienna, which said a lack of political will in Dnestr jeopardised a political settlement.

Johnson also criticised a memorandum Moldova and Dnestr drafted last June for a long-term settlement. He said its provisions, as they stand, did not reaffirm the OSCE principles of sovereignty and the territorial integrity of Moldova.
Litkai said Johnson's assessments were one-sided and undermined the authority of the OSCE as a mediator.
